messages.author: 732a31c2f861aaca
messages.subject: program Distance vs distsamp estimates
parts:
Hi I was wondering if someone could shed some light on differences in
density and detection probability between program Distance and the
distsamp function. I ran some analysis for ovenbird in Program
DISTANCE where I get a density of 10 birds/km sq., detection p 64% and
with the distsamp function I get density estimates of 18 birds/km sq.
detection p 36%. I think the difference in detection probability is
causing this discrepancy. I am also using the same distance bins and
detection function.
I don't expect the density estimates to be the same but I thought that
they should be somewhat closer. Any ideas on how I can figure out
what my be causing the difference in detection probability.

thanks,
Rob

messages.author: df74d6fccec2ff7e
messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] Re: program Distance vs distsamp estimates
parts:
Hi Rob,

I made the comparison again with simulated point transect data and the half-normal detection function, and the results are the same:

                    density       sigma
    Truth          15.00         25.00
    unmarked   14.23         25.18
    DISTANCE 14.23         25.18

The R code (lifted from unmarked's unitTests) is below. My suspicion is that the discrepancy you found has to do with specifying either "AREA" or "EFFORT" in DISTANCE. For example, did you specify how much area was surveyed (including points with no detections)? I would check that and then try ignoring the EFFORT option.

Please let us know if you get to the bottom of this.

Richard




Simulation code:

simPt <- function(lambda=5, sigma=20, npts=100,
    breaks=seq(0, 50, by=10))
{     
    radius <- max(breaks)
    A <- (2*radius)^2 / 10000 # Area (ha) of square containing circle
    y1 <- numeric(0)
    pt <- character(0)
    y2 <- matrix(NA, npts, length(breaks)-1)
    labs <- c(letters, paste(letters, letters, sep=""))
    for(i in 1:npts) {
        M <- rpois(1, lambda * A) # Individuals within the square
        # coordinates of each individual
        xy <- cbind(x=runif(M, -radius, radius), y=runif(M, -radius, radius))
       
        # Distances from each point
        d <- apply(xy, 1, function(x) sqrt(x[1]^2 + x[2]^2))
        d <- d[d <= radius]

        # Detection process
        if(length(d)) {
            p <- exp(-d^2 / (2 * sigma^2)) # half-normal
            d <- d[rbinom(length(d), 1, p) == 1]
            y1 <- c(y1, d)
            pt <- c(pt, rep(labs[i], length(d)))
            y2[i,] <- table(cut(d, breaks, include.lowest=TRUE))
            }
        }
    return(list(y1=data.frame(pt, y1), y2=y2))
}




set.seed(3)

db <- seq(0, 50, by=10)

sim1 <- simPt(15, 25, 50,db)
str(sim1)

nrow(sim1$y1) == sum(sim1$y2) # Should be true

library(unmarked)

umf <- unmarkedFrameDS(y=sim1$y2, dist.breaks=db, survey="point", unitsIn="m")

(m1 <- distsamp(~1~1, umf))
exp(coef(m1)) # D=14.23371, sigma=25.177

write.table(sim1$y1, "sim1.txt", row.names=F, sep=",")

messages.author: df74d6fccec2ff7e
messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] Re: program Distance vs distsamp estimates
parts:
Hi Rob,

I probably can't help much from here on because I think these are DISTANCE issues, but I would suggest

1. In DISTANCE, specify the total area surveyed, especially if there were no detections at some points
2. In DISTANCE, make sure that your second-to-lowest "layer" distinguishes each point transect (not grid).

Also, I think if you are using effort in DISTANCE but not in unmarked, there are bound to be differences. My understanding was that effort was only needed if points were surveyed multiple times.

Best,
Richard

On Thu, Mar 3, 2011 at 1:31 PM, Rob Sparks <robas...@gmail.com> wrote:

area in my DISTANCE project but I don't think I should ignore effort
(number of points conducted along the point transect) and I still get
the same results.
I have run some analysis for Brown Creeper and MacGillivray's Warbler
and the distsamp density estimates are pretty close to the program
DISTANCE estimates.  So I am not sure what is going on.
 I will try to get to the bottom of this.

Rob

strata besides the one I was doing the comparison on. So now in
program DISTANCE I am only using the stratum of interest and that
brings the detection probability down to about 0.32 and a density of
11 so it seems more reasonable now.

Rob
